lbl.Gli strati accesi compaiono come eti: Active layers appear as labels at the top of the map and the legend at the bottom left explains their colours. Next to each layer, buttons let you move it up or down, centre the map on its data and change its colours; the “Search layer” field filters the list. You can turn on more than one to compare them, for example buildings and cadastre.
lbl.Gli strati molto densi (come le part: Very dense layers (such as cadastral parcels) look better with WMS: WFS download has a cap of 10,000 features.
lbl.Gli strati si ricordano da una visit: Layers are remembered from one visit to the next, in this browser. If a service stops responding, it stays in the list marked as “unavailable” and is not deleted.
lbl.Gli strati sono i temi che si posson: Layers are the themes that can be overlaid on the map. On the left a vertical bar has five tabs: “Basemap”, “Layers”, “RNDT”, “My layers” and “Filters”. The “Layers” tab opens a panel with the groups of layers (Boundaries, Buildings, Events, Monuments, PAI plan, Population, Terrain, Services, Road safety, Territory, Transport), always in alphabetical order: a click on the group opens it, and each layer has a box to turn it on or off. lbl.I dati aggiunti compaiono nel gruppo: Added data appear in the “RNDT” group of the layers bar, and also among the Topics of the Info sheet. Each layer has the eye icon to turn it on or off and the bin to remove it. They are saved automatically and, when you reopen the map, they come back in place, on or off as you left them. Next to the name, “this session only” warns that the layer could not be saved.

lbl.I servizi aggiunti restano salvati n: Added services stay saved in the browser (up to fifty): a click on a row puts them back on the map, the bin removes them from the list. For protected services there are user and password fields, which stay in memory only while the page is open: when you reopen it the service shows a padlock and the password has to be entered again. For ArcGIS REST you can paste a token into the address. Data are shown within the Palermo area and the added layers appear under “Layers on the map”, with checkbox, opacity and arrows for the order.
lbl.Per provare subito il tab, sono già: To try the tab right away, a few examples are already loaded: some XYZ services, the WMS services of the Municipality of Palermo (Sispi) and the ArcGIS REST services of the SITR of the Sicilian Region.

lbl.I tuoi file non stanno più qui: si c: Your files are no longer here: they are loaded from the tree of the “My layers” group (the load icon next to “My data”) and appear in the same group, together with the XYZ, WMS, WMTS, WFS and ArcGIS REST services added by address, also with user and password. “Load a file from your computer” accepts: GeoJSON, KML, KMZ, GPX, Shapefile (a zip file that also includes the .prj) and CSV with latitude and longitude columns. GeoJSON and CSV must be in WGS84. Of each file only the features inside the Municipality of Palermo are kept, and a layer is saved up to 5 MB: beyond that, it only lasts while the page is open. You can also paste an https address in the “From a web address” field of “My data”: for a Google Sheets sheet, first share it with “Anyone with the link” (Viewer role) and remember the lat and lon columns; the file, at most 10 MB, is a copy that does not update itself.

lbl.Il pulsante con la tabella, nella ba: The table button, in the toolbar at the top right, opens the “Data table” from the bottom: the rows of the active layers, one tab per layer, like an attribute table. It shows the information loaded in the current view, so moving or zooming the map updates it; on a smartphone the button is in the “Layers” sheet. A layer that is switched off has no tab.
lbl.Per scegliere cosa vedere ci sono qu: Four selection tools choose what to see: “Click” picks one feature, “Box” and “Polygon” pick those inside the area you draw, “Area” picks those inside a district, a neighbourhood or a UPL. “Back to the view” returns to the rows visible on the map. The “Filter the rows” field searches the text, the column heading sorts, and the “Columns” menu shows, hides and moves columns.
lbl.Le caselle scelgono righe e colonne: The checkboxes choose the rows and columns to export; the CSV or GeoJSON button shows how many rows and columns will be written (for example “33 × 15”) and adds the layer's source and licence. Export is enabled for the City's open data whose licence allows it, such as road accidents and road safety; for the other layers, and for those you add yourself, the button stays off. The geometry of tiled layers is simplified: for precise data use the CSV.

The same goes for urban rail: every day the site checks the Trenitalia GTFS feed and, when a new version is published, stations, lines and timetables are replaced. If the feed in use has expired, the map says so.

pres.perche.diff.cap: Comparison between PalermoHub and Palermo Digital Twin
pres.perche.dt.h: Palermo Digital Twin is a workbench
pres.perche.dt.p1: It starts from the opposite question: "What is here?"
pres.perche.dt.p2: A single map, many layers you switch on and off: cadastre, zoning plan, population, buildings, relief, public transport, heat islands, hydrogeological risk, monuments, historical maps, municipal offices and more. One click on a point and the place card opens, bringing together all the data for that address.
pres.perche.dt.p3: But it is not only for looking, it is for working. Students, professionals and technicians can bring their own data onto the map and use it together with the layers already there, as in QGIS: just connect a source or drag a file, with nothing to install.
pres.perche.dt.p4: And the workbench takes its material from the library's shelves: all the Digital Twin data come from PalermoHub.
pres.perche.h: Why a new map, if PalermoHub already exists?
pres.perche.hub.p1: Each map is a work in its own right, with its own theme, source, author and year.
pres.perche.hub.p2: It works very well when the question is: "Is there a map on this topic?"
pres.perche.hub.p4: The limit is structural: each map lives on its own. To know what happens at a precise point of the city (which cadastral parcel it is, which zoning of the PRG, whether there are hydrogeological constraints, how hot it gets in summer) you have to open several maps, in several tabs, and compare the results by hand.
pres.perche.hub.tip: Open PalermoHub, the catalogue of maps of Palermo and Sicily (opens in a new tab)
pres.perche.p1: A fair question, and we asked it ourselves. 😁 PalermoHub has existed for years and collects hundreds of maps about Palermo, Sicily and even a few national ones. Why build something else?
pres.perche.p2: The short answer: PalermoHub and Palermo Digital Twin do not do the same job.
pres.perche.r01.d: A single integrated map of the city
pres.perche.r03.d: Many layers that can be combined in the same view
pres.perche.r04.d: The map itself: you search an address and click
pres.perche.r04.h: Search and filters (category, source, author, year, tag)
pres.perche.r05.d: Several overlaid themes, with a summary card of the place
pres.perche.r06.d: Loading of files (GeoJSON, KML/KMZ, GPX, Shapefile .zip, CSV with coordinates) and connection to WMS, WMTS, WFS, XYZ, REST services and Google Sheets, as in QGIS
pres.perche.r07.d: Built in, without opening other windows
pres.perche.r08.d: Data of the visible layers downloadable in several formats
pres.perche.r09.d: Consult, filter, add data, 3D view, RNDT plugin, Geoimage
pres.perche.r10.d: Interface designed for the phone (Map, Layers, Add, Menu tabs)
pres.perche.r11.d: Dedicated page with date, link to the original and licence for each source
pres.perche.unire.p1: Because they serve different purposes, and each works better this way.
pres.perche.unire.p2: PalermoHub remains the place to experiment, to tell a story on a theme, to publish a new map without having to fit it into a larger system.
pres.perche.unire.p3: The Digital Twin is where the data meet, where a map stops being an image to look at and becomes a tool to answer concrete questions about a place.
pres.perche.unire.p4: The two feed each other: every new map published on PalermoHub can become a layer of the Digital Twin, and every Digital Twin layer is backed by work already published and documented.

lbl.Sui layer a punti il colore non è l': On point layers colour is not the only cue: each layer has its own shape or icon, the same on the map, in the legend and in the hover box. MEF properties show a euro icon, and architectural barriers have one icon per group (historic route, city street, square, green area, museum…). Schools, polling stations, fuel stations, charging points, drinking fountains and monumental trees show a graduation cap, a check mark, a pump, a plug, a drop and a tree, in the colour of the type, brand or status. Municipal office sites carry a building icon at the centre of the ring: the bigger it is, the more offices it hosts. Monuments have one icon per category: church, colonnade, theatre, house, building, palette, book, tree, market, ruins, shield or pin. Accidents, stops and commuting stay circles. This keeps themes apart when printing in black and white or with colour-vision difficulties.
lbl.Il pulsante con il fumetto, nella ba: The speech-bubble button in the toolbar at the top right, or the “Talia” tab of the right-hand bar, opens Talia, the assistant that answers questions about the app, its layers and its functions. You type the question in the field at the bottom and press “Send”; on opening, Talia also offers a few questions to tap. Answers do not come from an external service: they are drawn from the site’s guide, in the language of the app, and above each answer is the title of the entry it comes from. “Read more” expands a long answer; if it finds nothing, Talia says so and suggests similar questions; the bin button clears the conversation.
lbl.Sotto la risposta compaiono dei puls: Below the answer there are buttons that let you act without searching the menus. A button with a layer’s name, such as “Charging points”, turns that layer on or off. When the layer has filters, the filter buttons appear, grouped (for the charging points: “Status” with “Available”, “Charging” and “Inactive”; “Current” with “Alternating current (AC, slow)” and “Direct current (DC, fast)”): one click leaves only that item on the map, “Show all” removes every filter. Choosing items from different groups leaves only the elements that meet all of them; the “On the map” line sums up the active filters and the legend on the map updates accordingly. Other buttons open the sheet of a place that was found, a panel tab or the related guide entry.
lbl.A sinistra la mappa con lo strato Co: On the left the map with the Charging points layer on and only the available chargers highlighted; on the right the Talia panel with the answer about charging points, the layer button and the “Status” and “Current” filter buttons, with “Available” pressed and the line “On the map: Status: Available”.

lbl.Nella pagina iniziale del sito, nell: On the home page of the site, in the section “What you can switch on”, the “Guided paths” are fourteen ready-made themes: Risks and climate, Hazard, exposure and risk, Schools and neighbourhoods, Mobility, A city in transformation, Public works in the pipeline, Heritage and greenery, Urban planning, Road safety, Who commutes, An accessible city, Public property and Vehicles on the move (two paths: flat map and tilted map). Each card says what the theme is about and which layers it includes.
lbl.Il pulsante «Apri la mappa» apre la: The “Open the map” button opens the map with those layers already switched on and the legends already active on the map; the “Urban planning” path also opens it centred on an area of Palermo. Once open, the layers can be switched off, on and changed as usual. To pick layers one by one there is the “Layer catalogue”, further down the same page.
